instructions: The day before, or at least 8 hours ahead: stir the 1 1/2 tbsp espresso powder into 3/4 cup hot water in a shallow bowl. Stir in 1 1/2 tbsp of the rum and let it cool to room temperature.

Bring about 1 inch of water to a gentle simmer in a saucepan. Separate the 3 eggs and put the yolks in a heatproof bowl that sits on the pan without touching the water. Keep the whites for another use.

Add the 6 tbsp sugar to the yolks. Set the bowl over the pan and whisk constantly for 8 to 10 minutes, until the mixture is pale and a little thick. You're cooking it to 160°F, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Rub a drop between your fingers: it's ready when there's no grit and it falls from the whisk in a ribbon that sits on top for a second.
Take the bowl off the pan and keep whisking for 2 minutes, so it cools a little.
In a large bowl, beat the cold mascarpone with the remaining 1 1/2 tbsp rum on medium speed until smooth, about 30 seconds. Beat in the yolk mixture until there are no streaks.

In another bowl, whip the 1 cup cold cream to stiff peaks, 2 to 3 minutes. Fold half of it into the mascarpone, then fold in the rest. Stop as soon as there are no streaks. Any longer and the cream turns grainy.

Dip 12 of the ladyfingers into the coffee one at a time, about 1 second on each side, and lay them in a single layer in an 8 inch square dish. Break a few to fill the gaps. Don't soak them, or the tiramisu will be soggy.
Spread half the cream over the ladyfingers.
Dip the last 12 ladyfingers the same way and lay them over the cream. Spread the rest of the cream on top and smooth it out.
Cover the dish and chill for at least 8 hours, or overnight.
Right before serving, dust the 1 1/2 tbsp cocoa over the top through a small strainer. Cut it into squares. This makes 8 pieces.
advance_prep_notes: Make the tiramisu the day before, or at least 8 hours ahead, so it sets in the fridge.
method_notes: Both layer quickly dipped ladyfingers with a mascarpone cream, finish with cocoa and chill before serving. Natasha's Kitchen (the lead) cooks the yolks and sugar over simmering water to 160°F, beats them into mascarpone with rum, folds in whipped cream and adds rum to the coffee, then chills it at least 8 hours. GialloZafferano uses raw yolks and whites beaten with sugar instead of cream, with no alcohol, and advises pasteurized eggs. This is half the lead in an 8 inch square dish, with instant espresso for the coffee and dark rum where the lead uses golden rum.
